key: And it was so from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel unto this day.
s: After the rout of the Amalekite raiders, David rules that the men who guarded the baggage share the spoil with those who fought; Rashi, on 30:25, reads the Hebrew wording as reaching back in time, since Abraham had already set this rule.

evidence.gloss: It does not say ‘onward’ but ‘and upward’ [that is, before]: Abraham had already set this statute (Genesis 14:24), ‘save only that which the young men have eaten’, those who sat by the baggage, ‘and the portion of the men’, those who went to war.

reason: verse.js ok, ref 1 Samuel 30:25 and at [261,25] match. Plain sense faithful: 30:1 to 30:24 tell the Amalekite raid, its rout and David’s ruling that those who tarried by the baggage share alike; no four-word run from the key. Read Rashi, Radak and Metzudat David across chapter 30. Rashi’s own words on מהיום ההוא ומעלה say the text says ‘and upward’, not ‘onward’, because Abraham had already instituted this statute; the sentence’s ‘reaching back in time’ is exactly that, and it says ‘the Hebrew wording’ since the JPS key prints ‘forward’. Metzudat David reads the verse as David fixing it for all time, a complement rather than a contrary reading, so one commentator suffices.
